title: Carotid and vertebral artery disease and dissection

steps.tx: Spontaneous dissection of the extracranial **internal carotid artery** represents a major cause of ischaemic stroke in young adults. The classic clinical presentation consists of the diagnostic triad of sudden unilateral frontotemporal or neck pain, a painful partial **Horner syndrome** lacking facial anhidrosis, and delayed cerebral or retinal ischaemic symptoms within several hours to days.

steps.tx: Spontaneous **vertebral artery dissection** typically targets the mobile V3 horizontal loop segment as the vessel winds around the **atlas loop** at the suboccipital triangle. Patients experience severe ipsilateral occipitonuchal headache and neck stiffness, followed hours or days later by brainstem or cerebellar stroke manifestations including lateral medullary ischaemia.

steps.tx: High-resolution cross-sectional magnetic resonance imaging provides non-invasive diagnostic confirmation of cervical arterial dissection. Axial fat-saturated **T1-weighted** magnetic resonance imaging exquisitely reveals an eccentric crescentic hyperintense **intramural hematoma** surrounding a narrowed eccentric arterial flow void, confirming acute or subacute subadventitial dissection.

steps.tx: Initial antithrombotic management of acute extracranial **cervical artery dissection** focuses on secondary embolic prevention. Randomised clinical data from the CADISS and TREAT-CAD trials establish equivalent clinical efficacy between antiplatelet agents and therapeutic **anticoagulation**, demonstrating no significant differences in stroke recurrence or overall survival outcomes.

steps.tx: An intimal fibrovascular anomaly known as a **Carotid web** arises as a shelf-like projection along the posterior wall of the **internal carotid** bulb. This projection causes localized flow stagnation and recirculation, generating microthrombi that predispose young patients to recurrent embolic strokes despite standard single antiplatelet therapy.

steps.tx: Revascularization strategies for symptomatic high-grade atherosclerotic stenosis balance clinical and perioperative procedural risks. While conventional surgery remains standard, **Carotid artery stenting** represents a proven therapeutic alternative for individuals presenting with surgically hostile neck anatomy, prior cervical radiation injury, or high surgical contraindications to open **carotid endarterectomy**.

steps.tx: Severe proximal stenosis or occlusion of the prevertebral subclavian artery precipitates **Subclavian steal syndrome**. Vigorous upper extremity exercise creates a marked pressure gradient, inducing retrograde reversal of flow down the ipsilateral **vertebral artery** to supply the working arm at the expense of brainstem and cerebellar perfusion.

steps.tx: Non-atherosclerotic vascular dysplasia known as **Fibromuscular dysplasia** predominantly affects young to middle-aged female patients. Medial fibroplasia accounts for over 80% of cases, yielding the pathognomonic string-of-beads angiographic contour along the mid and distal segments of the extracranial **internal carotid** and renal arteries.
